steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on a measurement-based small-scale channel model for sub-6 GHz RIS-assisted communications. Briefly introduce reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, review the existing RIS channel models and the gap in empirical small-scale fading work, and summarize our measurement campaign and main findings.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. What an RIS is and why it matters
2. Existing RIS channel models and the missing empirical work
3. This study: measurement campaign, scenarios, modes, findings

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. RIS background
- reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS): promising solution for future wireless communications (cite)
- nearly-passive 2D metasurface, programmable unit cells embedded periodically (cite)
- unit cells: individually diffuse scatterers, jointly beamforming in desired direction -> energy-efficient alternative to large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)
- adaptive control of propagation of electromagnetic (EM) waves -> better channel quality, even shape communication-friendly channel (cite)

2. Existing channel models
- some deterministic and statistical models so far
- RIS-aided bipartite cascaded Rician channel (cite): transmitter (Tx)-RIS and RIS-receiver (Rx) channels with different K-factors (KFs); tight upper bound on ergodic spectral efficiency
- three-dimensional (3D) geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM), inspired by 3GPP framework, generalized to RIS-assisted channels (cite); Tx-Rx small-scale fading parameters extrapolated to RIS cascaded channel
- 3D cylindrical model -> theoretical 3D RIS-assisted MIMO channel model (cite): line-of-sight (LOS), single-bounced and double-bounced modes
- gap: no empirical small-scale fading characterization from real measurements

3. This study
- small-scale statistical channel characteristics of RIS-assisted system; measurement campaign at 2.6 GHz
- scenarios: outdoor, indoor, outdoor-to-indoor (O2I)
- modes: intelligent reflection with RIS (IRWR), specular reflection with RIS (SRWR), without RIS (WR)
- statistical channel model for small-scale propagation of EM waves
- global, inter-cluster, intra-cluster statistics from measured data
- finding: KF of IRWR much higher than SRWR, WR
- cluster root mean square delay spread (RMS DS): IRWR focuses signal energy, reduces time dispersion

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has recently been seen as one of the promising solutions for the future of wireless communications. In general, an RIS is a nearly-passive two-dimensional metasurface, where several programmable unit cells are embedded periodically. The unit cells act independently as diffuse scatterers but together they perform beamforming in a desired direction, so they can be seen as an energy-efficient alternative to large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. Since they can control the propagation of electromagnetic (EM) waves adaptively, RISs can improve the channel quality or even shape a channel that is communication-friendly.

So far, some works have developed deterministic and statistical channel models. The RIS-aided bipartite cascaded Rician channel was introduced in one work. It is made of the transmitter (Tx)-RIS and RIS-receiver (Rx) channels, which have different K -factors (KFs). The authors of that work derived a tight upper bound on the ergodic spectral efficiency. In another work, a three-dimensional (3D) geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM), inspired by the existing 3GPP standardized modeling framework, was generalized so it could be applied to RIS-assisted channels. In particular, the traditional Tx-Rx small-scale fading parameters were extrapolated to an RIS cascaded channel. Based on a 3D cylindrical model, the authors of a third work proposed a theoretical 3D RIS-assisted MIMO channel model, which considered line-of-sight (LOS) and also the single-bounced and double-bounced modes. Although the theoretical modeling of RIS-aided channels has been studied in the literature, the empirical characterization of small-scale fading based on real measurements has surprisingly not been reported.

In this study, we investigate the small-scale statistical channel characteristics of an RIS-assisted wireless system, based on a channel measurement campaign done at 2.6 GHz. We consider three typical communication scenarios: outdoor, indoor and outdoor-to-indoor (O2I) environments. In each scenario we investigate three propagation modes: intelligent reflection with RIS (IRWR), specular reflection with RIS (SRWR), and without RIS (WR). We formulate a statistical channel model to describe the small-scale propagation behavior of EM waves. Then, using the measured channel data, we characterize the global, inter-cluster, and intra-cluster statistics. We find that the KF of the IRWR mode is much higher than for the SRWR and WR modes. We also evaluate the root mean square delay spread (RMS DS) of a cluster, and it shows that the IRWR mode can effectively focus the signal energy and reduce the time dispersion.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has recently been considered one of the promising solutions for underpinning the future of wireless communications [1,2,3]. Generally, an RIS refers to a nearly-passive two-dimensional metasurface in which several programmable unit cells are embedded periodically [4,5,6]. By acting independently as diffuse scatterers but jointly performing beamforming in a desired direction, these unit cells can be regarded as an energy-efficient alternative to large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. Thanks to their ability to control the propagation of electromagnetic (EM) waves adaptively, RISs can improve the channel quality or even shape a communication-friendly channel [7,8,9].

Up to now, some works have developed deterministic and statistical channel models. The RIS-aided bipartite cascaded Rician channel was introduced in [10]; it consists of the transmitter (Tx)-RIS and RIS-receiver (Rx) channels with different K -factors (KFs). The authors of [10] derived a tight upper bound on the ergodic spectral efficiency. In [11], a three-dimensional (3D) geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM), inspired by the existing 3GPP standardized modeling framework, was generalized to RIS-assisted channels. In particular, the traditional Tx-Rx small-scale fading parameters were extrapolated to an RIS cascaded channel. Based on a 3D cylindrical model, the authors of [12] proposed a theoretical 3D RIS-assisted MIMO channel model that considered line-of-sight (LOS) as well as the single-bounced and double-bounced modes. Surprisingly, although the theoretical modeling of RIS-aided channels has been investigated in the literature, the empirical characterization of small-scale fading based on real measurements has not been reported.

In this study, we investigate the small-scale statistical channel characteristics of an RIS-assisted wireless system based on a channel measurement campaign performed at 2.6 GHz. Three typical communication scenarios are considered, namely outdoor, indoor and outdoor-to-indoor (O2I) environments. In each scenario, three propagation modes are investigated: intelligent reflection with RIS (IRWR), specular reflection with RIS (SRWR), and without RIS (WR). We formulate a statistical channel model to describe the small-scale propagation behavior of EM waves. Then, based on the measured channel data, we characterize the global, inter-cluster, and intra-cluster statistics. We find that the KF of the IRWR mode is much higher than that of the SRWR and WR modes. Moreover, the root mean square delay spread (RMS DS) of a cluster is evaluated, revealing that the IRWR mode can effectively focus the signal energy and reduce the time dispersion.
